doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: His rehearsal band at the union
summary: The no-pressure rehearsal band he led with top players.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: What kind of gig do you like to play now that has sort of no pressure. Like when you’re doing “Chicago” every night you just have to be so focused. What kind of gig is the total opposite of that for you?

Boy that’s a good question man. Well actually I had a rehearsal band with some good arrangements and that was fun. I would call a rehearsal, I’d call up the guys, great players, everybody would always say yes I’ll be there, for no money, for two hours maybe in between shows. And we’d play whatever I’d call up. I was the leader. Let’s

play #23 you know. And man, like it was, after that two hours, first of all everybody always showed up. Nobody canceled or anything. I mean great players man. Bobby Porcelli, great alto player. He would get the saxophones. And man like just all great players man. And they would want to play longer. I only had the room for two hours. It was at the union by the way, which is closed, our union is closed. We’re waiting for it to open so I can bring in my band again and rehearse. Because they have a great room with drums and, you know, not only me everybody wants to do it. But then I would play with other bands too, rehearsal bands, that was fun. There was no pressure. You know you’re sight reading but it doesn’t matter. There’s no audience you’re just by yourselves playing. There might be a few people hanging out. But that was fun. But to tell you the truth man I want to go on a gig and play some tunes man. I just want to play “All the Things You Are.” You know. I mean you know I just want to play some tunes man, good tunes. Just ding-ding-a-ding.
Come on up to Utica and we’ll play some dang-dang-a-dang.
